content.title: This dog breed remains favorite in U.S., but a challenger emerges
content.text: U.S. NewsPublished: Mar. 19, 2026, 12:06 a.m.The French bulldog is the most popular breed in the U.S.AP Photo/Mary Altaffer, FileBy Cliff Pinckard, cleveland.comNEW YORK — When it comes to dog breeds, “Vive la France!”The French bulldog is the most popular breed in the U.S. for the fourth straight year, according to registration statistics from the American Kennel Club.At No. 2 is the Labrador retriever; No. 3 is the golden retriever; and No. 4 is the German shepherd.The Dachshund landed at No. 5, the highest it’s been ranked since 2003, according to the AKC.“While the French bulldog is a wonderful companion for many, it is not a ‘one size fits all’ breed,” Gina DiNardo, AKC President and CEO, said in a statement. “Popularity does not mean it’s right for everyone.”According to PetMD.com, the French bulldog is prone to more than 20 health issues, with a major issue being breathing because of its flattened snout. Treating breathing issues often involves surgery. French bulldogs also are sensitive to heat.“Another breed to watch this year is the curious, spunky Dachshund,” DiNardo said. “The breed has hovered in the top 10 most popular breeds for many years, and it’s no surprise that it’s back in the top five. Dachshunds are very intelligent, excellent problem solvers and adorable.”RECOMMENDEDA purebred Dachshund also can develop health issues, most likely with the spine, PetMD.com says.“As with any breed, we can’t stress enough the importance of doing your research to find the right breed for your lifestyle and to ensure that you’re getting a well-bred dog from a responsible breeder,” DiNardo said.The poodle fell out of the top five but still finished at No. 6. Also in the top 10 were the beagle (7), Rottweiler (8), German shorthaired pointer (9) and the bulldog (10).Cliff Pinckard has been with The Plain Dealer/cleveland.com since 1999.
